source.title: Stochastic batch size for adaptive regularization in deep network optimization
source.authors: Kensuke Nakamura; Stefano Soatto; Byung-Woo Hong

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates a new stochastic per-parameter batch-size method and compares validation accuracy across batch sizes and optimization methods, bearing on the optimizer, batch-size, and dropout versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation-accuracy results for its own method, SGD, Adam and other optimizer or regularizer comparisons. Cited findings from prior work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The paper's own SGD-versus-adaptive-optimizer and dropout comparisons test V4 and V6. Its batch-size sweeps bear on V5, but the text does not establish the fixed epoch budgets required to interpret that version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: their stochastic batch-size method improves classification generalization, especially with fewer training examples, without additional computational cost. These are the authors' claims; the explicit computational argument concerns matching SGD's back-propagation cost, rather than a reported runtime benchmark.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces stochastic per-parameter batch sizes as adaptive regularization and evaluates validation accuracy against SGD and other methods; it does not test the original claim's interventions or measures directly.
record.method_sensitivity: Validation accuracy varies with learning-rate schedule, batch size, momentum, training-set fraction, dataset, architecture, and the proposed method's local and global update-probability parameters.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed stochastic per-parameter batch method improves validation accuracy over baseline SGD, including on partial training sets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive stochastic per-parameter batch sizes can improve image-classification validation accuracy over SGD under the tested recipe.

record.problems: Results use validation accuracy rather than test error; the reported comparisons do not measure train-test gaps. The batch-size/momentum choices vary together in Table 2, complicating attribution to batch size alone. Error bars are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2's remaining batch-size/momentum combinations and Table 5's other batch sizes and maximum-accuracy results were omitted to stay within 60 rows; the selected rows retain representative conditions for each tested version. Table 4's partial-training comparisons of the proposed method versus SGD were omitted because they test the new method rather than the mapped claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and the paired comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Language benchmarks, broader optimizer tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and equal or better adaptive-method training performance.
The fixed epoch-budget requirement is undocumented. Language models, longer training, warmup, and controlled learning-rate scaling or normalization changes are not tested.

Dropout-rate tuning, fully connected classifiers, a controlled training-set-size sweep with dropout, underfitting from excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and ranking against alternative measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: RMSProp-versus-SGD comparisons: VGG11 mean/max 88.55/89.42% versus 92.03/92.48%; ResNet18 91.11/91.88% versus 94.89/95.16%. These additionally support V4 under the reported limited tuning.
Epoch counts and confirmation that compared batch sizes receive equal epoch budgets are unavailable in the supplied text, preventing a firm V5 verdict.

record.verdict_notes: No original-source exclusion applies. Validation accuracy measures held-out performance, but validation-based hyperparameter selection is not an independent final test. No V5 label is assigned because equal epoch budgets are undocumented. Remaining Table 2 conditions and Table 5 batch sizes and maximum-accuracy results are explicitly declared omitted, so they are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and generalization on natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Language benchmarks; broader optimizer tuning; switching from Adam to SGD; decoupled weight decay; word-level language models.
Language models; extended training; warmup and learning-rate scaling; comparisons under a fixed epoch budget are not explicitly detailed.
Very small training sets and removing dropout together with weight decay under data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
